items.title: Bara Hari returns with new single ‘Iron Heart’
items.summary: Los Angeles dark electro-pop artist Bara Hari released the single "Iron Heart" on 22 October 2026, produced by Ian Flux at Monican Audio.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles dark electro-pop artist Bara Hari released the single “Iron Heart” on 22 October 2026. It is the project’s first new single since “A Flower in His Garden” in August 2025, and leans further into alternative rock than Bara Hari’s earlier synth-driven work.

“Iron Heart” was produced and mixed by Ian Flux at Monican Audio, with live drums from Lorne Walker. Bara Hari founder Sam Franco wrote the track about personal accountability within the difficulties of a relationship, describing the record as a step into new territory: “I experimented with some new sounds.”

“Iron Heart” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and streaming platforms.

About Bara Hari

Bara Hari is the Los Angeles-based project of Sam Franco. Side-Line has covered the act since 2021, starting with the single “Weapon” in March, the EP announcement “Dark New Day” with the video for “Ugly on the Inside” in May, and the video for “Artificial” in October, all released through Re:Mission Entertainment. Side-Line premiered the video for “Tempest” in November 2022; an acoustic version of the song followed in 2024. Bara Hari continued with the single and video “Violence Rising” in January 2023, the single and video “House of the Devil” in March 2023, and the debut album “Lesser Gods” in May 2023. Re:Mission Entertainment has also included Bara Hari on its free annual label compilations. The single “There Goes That Dream,” featuring genCAB, followed in 2024, and “A Flower in His Garden” in August 2025. “Iron Heart,” out 22 October 2026, is Bara Hari’s latest single.

items.title: Iara Naga release debut single ‘Big Fish’
items.summary: Iara Naga, the new industrial darkwave duo of Shonalika and Danny Sanchez, released the debut single "Big Fish" on Gasolina Recordings.
items.fullText:
Iara Naga, the new industrial darkwave duo of Shonalika and Danny Sanchez, released its debut single, “Big Fish”, on 22 October 2026 via Gasolina Recordings. The London and Brighton-based project formed in summer 2026 after the pair’s previous band, Death Drive, came to an end, and “Big Fish” is the first release under the new name.

The name Iara Naga comes from shape-shifting figures in Indian and Brazilian folklore, reflecting Shonalika and Sanchez’s own heritage. “Big Fish” was produced by the duo and mixed by Jack Milwaukee, who records as M!R!M. The track addresses identity, marginalisation and the abuse of power within niche music scenes. Iara Naga build the song on industrial darkwave production that also pulls in synthpop, punk and percussive EBM elements.

“Big Fish” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and streaming platforms.

About Iara Naga

Iara Naga is the industrial darkwave project of Shonalika and Danny Sanchez, formed in London and Brighton in summer 2026 after the end of the pair’s previous band, Death Drive, a London darkwave duo. The project’s name draws on shape-shifting figures from Indian and Brazilian folklore, reflecting the members’ own backgrounds. “Big Fish,” released 22 October 2026 on Gasolina Recordings, is Iara Naga’s debut single, produced by the duo and mixed by Jack Milwaukee (M!R!M), and addresses identity, marginalisation and the abuse of power in niche music scenes.

items.title: Dead Astronauts Dig Into Romantic Ruin on New Album “Shallow Grave”
items.summary: Shaking under spotlight Melting in a silent fright Breaking just to do what’s right We all change into glistening things Humanity has developed an astonishing capacity for turning its most… The post Dead Astronauts Dig Into Romantic Ruin on New Album “Shallow
items.fullText:
Shaking under spotlight

Melting in a silent fright

Breaking just to do what’s right

We all change into glistening things

Humanity has developed an astonishing capacity for turning its most elementary desires into elaborate forms of psychological torture. We fall in love, become possessive, mistake dependency for devotion, and eventually discover that the person who once seemed capable of saving us has acquired an intimate knowledge of precisely where to insert the knife. Entire industries have been built around these spectacular failures of judgment, from popular music and psychotherapy to greeting cards and divorce litigation. The absurdity would be hilarious if the consequences weren’t so frequently catastrophic.

For the past decade, Dead Astronauts have occupied a curious intersection of darkwave, synthwave, gothic rock, and cinematic electronic music, producing records increasingly preoccupied with the psychological debris of modern existence. Now operating as the duo of Jared Kyle and Slade Templeton, the project has developed an international following through releases on Cold Transmission Music and NewRetroWave. Following Ghosts, their fifth studio album, Shallow Grave, takes their longstanding fascination with memory, obsession, and mortality into considerably more uncomfortable territory.

Across Shallow Grave, Kyle and Templeton bring together the romantic fatalism of gothic rock, the propulsive mechanics of post-punk, and the synthetic architecture of darkwave, allowing abrasion and melody to coexist within an increasingly disturbed vision of modern existence. Their subject matter ranges from private emotional catastrophe to collective moral collapse, held together by the uncomfortable recognition that human beings possess an almost supernatural ability to repeat their worst mistakes.

The album opens with An Intro, a whispered poem delivered over atmospheric synthesizer pads and disquieting electronic textures. The words possess the dreadful intimacy of somebody revealing a secret they have kept for far too many years, while the surrounding electronics establish a sense of apprehension that carries into the record’s first proper song. It’s a suitably theatrical beginning, suggesting that whatever follows will involve several questionable decisions and the sort of emotional damage that rarely responds to conventional treatment.

Bodies immediately introduces the album’s central preoccupation with violence and its psychological consequences. Brooding post-punk rhythms accompany images of manipulation, physical suffering, and memories that have acquired an independent existence. Somewhere between the silver screen and the spectacle of suffering, other people’s pain has become entertainment, and the individuals responsible for manufacturing it seem remarkably pleased with themselves. There’s a vicious little observation buried here about our appetite for watching people get torn apart, especially when the spectacle comes equipped with a sufficiently attractive soundtrack.

The title track, Shallow Grave, takes the proceedings into the miserable romantic territory where affection becomes another method of self-destruction. A woman seeks comfort in a relationship whose emotional foundations appear considerably less stable than either participant would care to acknowledge. The repeated assurances of devotion acquire the ghastly sweetness of a poisoned valentine, while the melodic restraint gives the lyrics room to expose the absurdity of loving somebody so completely that annihilation begins to resemble companionship. The prospect of digging a hole for two suggests that romance has officially exhausted its more conventional possibilities.

Get Lost continues this examination of emotional captivity through imagery of mechanical dependence, bodily deterioration, and surrender. Its driving post-punk foundation accompanies a speaker who recognizes the destructive nature of an attachment yet remains prepared to disappear into it. The relationship operates with the efficiency of a machine designed to consume its participants, while the repeated questioning of what remains after someone has finished dismantling your identity gives the song its disturbing emotional weight. There is an awful lot of romantic literature devoted to the idea of losing oneself in love, and very little of it bothers to investigate who is responsible for cleaning up afterward.

With Glistening Things, the album develops a more grotesquely sensual fascination with physical transformation. Skin peels back, bones become objects of strange beauty, and suffering assumes the character of a horrible metamorphosis. The song’s uneasy romantic quality makes these images especially disturbing, suggesting that beauty and decay have been sharing an apartment for centuries without anybody bothering to introduce them. Beneath the delicate exterior lies a fascination with the biological machinery that allows us to experience love, desire, terror, and the bewildering spectacle of consciousness itself.

Who Kills Who expands the album’s concerns beyond individual suffering into the miserable business of organized oppression. Invisible authorities govern through dependency and fear, while the people struggling beneath them dream of freedom. Unfortunately, liberation carries its own terrible possibilities. The oppressed eventually acquire the weapons of their persecutors, and the cycle begins again with a fresh collection of enthusiastic participants. The song’s confrontational electronic attack gives this observation a bitter urgency, presenting human civilization as an endlessly recurring exercise in learning absolutely nothing from catastrophe.

That suspicion becomes considerably more personal on Stuck (In a Modern Day Cult), where psychological manipulation reduces the individual to a frightened collection of borrowed thoughts and impulses. Estrangement from one’s own body, invasive voices, and the desperate desire for human connection suggest a consciousness attempting to escape an elaborate system of coercion. The surrounding instability introduces the possibility that even one’s own perceptions can become unreliable, while the forces responsible for maintaining control appear reluctant to surrender their investment. Beneath the track’s sinister atmosphere lies a familiar modern predicament: the astonishing ease with which people can be persuaded to surrender their autonomy to anybody sufficiently skilled at exploiting their loneliness.

Make It Right introduces a domestic tragedy, following a woman who responds to an abusive man’s cruelty by arranging his permanent removal from the premises. Revenge, survival, and justice become hopelessly entangled as the lyrics describe a midnight confrontation and the secrecy surrounding its aftermath. The song possesses the uncomfortable moral energy of a crime committed after every reasonable alternative has apparently been exhausted. Here, violence becomes an instrument of deliverance, although the distinction between liberation and vengeance remains sufficiently murky to trouble even the most enthusiastic advocate of frontier justice.

By the time From Dust arrives, the album has exhausted most of humanity’s more intimate methods of destruction and turns its attention toward the collective predicament. A world in flames, the certainty of impermanence, and the possibility of companionship beyond physical existence form the basis of an existential meditation on our astonishing inability to learn from our mistakes. The line, “We all die young, with the light of the sun. We don’t think it through, just a thing we do,” captures the record’s fatalistic humour with almost embarrassing precision. We arrive without instructions, spend our allotted time enthusiastically damaging the furniture, and depart before anybody can explain what the hell was supposed to happen. Yet the invitation to face an uncertain future together introduces a curious tenderness into the proceedings. After an album occupied with manipulation, emotional deterioration, and the machinery of oppression, companionship survives as one of the few remaining consolations.

And because no respectable excursion through the darker corners of the human psyche should conclude without somebody turning up the drum machines, Dead Astronauts finish with Bodies (Dark Club Edition), an EBM-flavoured reconstruction of the earlier track. Its dancefloor emphasis transforms the original’s catalogue of violence and psychological wreckage into a muscular electronic stomper, giving the record a final burst of physical energy. One imagines the accumulated anxieties of the preceding songs being processed through a particularly unforgiving nightclub sound system, where existential dread becomes considerably easier to tolerate once the bass starts rearranging your internal organs.

Shallow Grave is out now via Cold Transmission Music. Listen to the album below, and order it here.

Perhaps the great cosmic joke is that we spend so much time worrying about our limited existence while behaving as though we have an unlimited supply of second chances. Shallow Grave finds Dead Astronauts examining that contradiction with morbidity, affection, and a distinctly unhealthy interest in the ways people manipulate, consume, and occasionally rescue one another. The human condition remains a spectacularly disorganized enterprise, although at least somebody has had the good sense to provide it with a decent bassline.

items.title: Chaos Tamed – Nordverk (Digital Album – I/O Music)
items.summary: Magnus Kalnins first gained recognition with his Future-Pop project Colony 5 before moving on to...
items.fullText:
Magnus Kalnins first gained recognition with his Future-Pop project Colony 5 before moving on to Chaos Tamed. The Swedish artist has now released his third album, featuring nine tracks.

“Nordverk” picks up where its predecessors left off, once again delivering a mature, intelligent composition whose strength lies more in its overall sound production than in its BPM. Atmosphere takes centre stage in a soundscape where Dark-Electro and EBM merge into a vintage-inspired sonic landscape, evoking the early work of Skinny Puppy, as well as Front Line Assembly and Neuroactive. I previously compared Chaos Tamed to Haujobb, and that comparison still holds some merit. However, Chaos Tamed is certainly no copy of these bands; it has its own distinct style and sonic DNA. This is the kind of album I associate more with the visual arts than with the dance floor, as its music lends itself to creating vivid mental images and enhancing a particular atmosphere.

“Nordverk” may not be my favorite Chaos Tamed album, but it is still well worth discovering and offers plenty of intriguing moments. (Rating:7½).

Listen to “Determination”:

About Chaos Tamed

Chaos Tamed is the solo project of Magnus Kalnins, a longtime member and songwriter of Swedish futurepop band Colony 5. The project began as a side venture during a hiatus from Colony 5 and has grown into an independent body of work, moving between EBM, IDM, dark electro and futurepop around ethereal, ghostly vocals over pulsing basslines and cinematic textures.

The debut Chaos Tamed album, “Shock Waves,” was released via I/O Music on November 9, 2023, and earned a nomination for Electronic Album of the Year at the GAFFA Awards in early 2024. The second album, “Elbrus”, followed on I/O Music on May 30, 2025, in digital and CD formats, and led to a 2025 Side-Line interview in which Kalnins described the project as more of a laboratory than a conventional band. The advance single “Destroyer” arrived in May 2026 ahead of “Nordverk,” the third Chaos Tamed album issued via I/O Music on July 24, 2026.

items.title: Substance Festival Returns to LA and SF This Weekend and Next with Drab Majesty, Cold Cave, Desire, and More!

items.fullText:
Substance Festival returns to California this weekend and next with a gathering of post-punk, darkwave, industrial, EBM, and synthpop artists spread across two cities and five nights. Los Angeles gets a takeover of The Belasco on Saturday, October 24, while San Francisco hosts four evenings at Great American Music Hall on October 22, 23, 29, and 30. Between Drab Majesty, A Split Second, Crash Course in Science, Desire, and Cold Cave performing Cremations, the calendar offers plenty of opportunities to rearrange one’s sleeping habits.

As in previous editions, Substance puts the relationships between generations within earshot. The electronic experiments that helped establish this music share a bill with artists pushing its rhythms, theatricality, and emotional extremes in fresh directions. There is considerable pleasure in recognizing those connections from the dance floor, particularly when an unfamiliar name on the timetable becomes the reason you arrive early.

The published timetables list start times only. 

Los Angeles

Saturday, October 24 — The Belasco

The Los Angeles edition packs three live stages and a DJ booth into one evening, with doors opening at 6:00 PM. The Belasco is located at 1050 South Hill Street, and the event is all ages.

The Chapel’s running order makes a strong case for arriving at the beginning and staying into the small hours. Philadelphia synth-punk experimenters Crash Course in Science, whose history reaches back to 1979, open the main stage; Spike Hellis, Madeline Goldstein, Buzz Kull, and Kontravoid carry the evening toward Belgian EBM pioneers A Split Second. Drab Majesty then take the final slot, with Deb Demure and Mona D’s expansive guitar melodies, synthesizers, and otherworldly presentation offering an appropriately ambitious destination.

There are good reasons to explore the other floors from the outset. Blone Noble opens The Sanctuary following the release of “Designer”, his art-rock collaboration with Dakota Blue, while XTR HUMAN brings the forceful EBM of his recent “Fake” single to The Chamber. Those early appointments leave plenty to discover before the later run of SRSQ, Void Vision, Zanias, Die Sexual, and Aux Animaux.

A little advance planning will help: Buzz Kull and SRSQ begin five minutes apart, while A Split Second and Zanias start within ten minutes of one another. After midnight, Vioflesh, a TR/ST DJ set, and Drab Majesty begin across the three live rooms within twenty minutes. The complete stage-by-stage schedule follows.

San Francisco

Great American Music Hall, at 859 O’Farrell Street, hosts Substance across two successive Thursday-and-Friday pairings. Doors open at 6:00 PM each night. Each bill has its own character, giving Bay Area audiences four different routes through the festival’s mix of electronic pop, body music, and post-punk.

Thursday, October 22

Opening night puts two important chapters of electronic music history at the top of the bill. Crash Course in Science bring the restless invention of Philadelphia’s late-1970s synth-punk underground, followed by A Split Second, whose 1986 single “Flesh” helped shape Belgian New Beat. The earlier sequence of God Tongue, Pink Stiletto, Vioflesh, and Automelodi makes this a full evening of discovery before those final appointments. For listeners drawn to the meeting point of experimental electronics and club music, Thursday is a particularly persuasive starting place.

Friday puts Aux Animaux, GHOST COP, and Zanias ahead of a substantial late-night stretch with Kontravoid, Buzz Kull, and TR/ST behind the decks. Kontravoid’s Sound of the Void, released October 2 through Artoffact, and Buzz Kull’s Deep Hate EP give the pairing fresh material to draw upon. Zanias adds another compelling voice to the evening: Alison Lewis’s work moves between coldwave, forceful electronics, and the emotional and political concerns explored on Cataclysm.

The second week turns toward the theatrical pleasures of electronic pop. Desire, the project of Megan Louise and Johnny Jewel, close the evening with their combination of cinematic synthesizers, disco, and romantic unease. Immediately before them, identical twins Elyse and Larena’s MOTHERMARY bring the art-pop sensibility introduced on their Italians Do It Better debut, I Am Your God. With Violet Thrones, CLUBDRUGS, Madeline Goldstein, and Sacred Skin filling the earlier hours, there is ample incentive to make a full night of it.

SRSQ, the project of Kennedy Ashlyn, provides an equally compelling reason to attend, bringing a powerful voice and a body of work that stretches between dream pop, shoegaze, and emotional directness. items.fullText:
Exhaustion has become such an ordinary feature of daily life that we have practically mistaken it for a personality. The calendar stays full, the messages keep coming, and the future starts to resemble a corridor lined with doors that have all been locked from the other side. Carry on long enough and even the promise of escape begins to sound like another item on the to-do list.

Louisville, Kentucky industrial punk trio VIRGIN BIRTH give that predicament a particularly bruising accompaniment with The Dead End, the title track from their newly released six-song EP, with a video by the band’s own Phillip Olympia. Their fascination with electronic music’s darker corners and punk’s abrasive economy takes an increasingly personal turn, bringing the effects of a deteriorating world into the cramped confines of an exhausted mind.

The song opens with eerie electronic tones before a sizzling hi-hat pattern ushers in a restless beat reminiscent of The Prodigy. A kick drum lands with a heavy thud beneath the percussion’s rapid shuffle, while growling guitars bear down on the arrangement. Their harsh attack against the programmed rhythm recalls Ministry’s Stigmata, giving the track a sense of force held to a precise, punishing tempo.

Olympia spits out the vocal with an acidic, grunge-inflected bite, his delivery recalling Trent Reznor’s agitated intimacy and Bill Leeb’s severity. Spoken-word murmurs and anxious synth pulses add to the discomfort, drawing the ear toward smaller disturbances within the mix. The hi-hats keep sizzling around that blunt kick, the guitars crowd the available space, and the voice sounds frayed by the machinery surrounding it.

Olympia’s visuals extend that unease through a largely monochrome collage of overlapping faces, cloud formations, blurred performance footage, and vintage exercise routines. Heads and hands leave smeared trails across the image as the musicians appear to split into multiple versions of themselves. Faces push toward the camera, lose definition, and disappear beneath another layer of movement, with occasional glimpses of instruments anchoring the confusion.

The exercise footage supplies a peculiar, bitter joke. Women in leotards work through synchronized routines, their carefully repeated movements carrying the familiar promise that enough effort will eventually make everything better. Against the song’s accumulating strain, that orderly exertion starts to resemble another exhausting obligation. The bodies keep moving, the beat keeps counting, and relief remains conspicuously absent.

Watch the video for The Dead End below:

VIRGIN BIRTH is comprised of Phillip Olympia on vocals, synthesizers, and drum machines; Jake Miller on guitars and synthesizers; and Matt Haas on bass. All three have deep roots in punk and indie rock, having played in various bands over the years. A shared appreciation for the industrial music of the 1980s and 1990s sparked conversations that eventually led to experiments with drum machines, synthesizers, and sampling.

Across The Dead End, their focus moves from the wider collapse examined on previous releases toward exhaustion, isolation, dread, and the private consequences of living with an ever-narrowing set of possibilities. The EP’s six songs offer industrial punk for a world running on its last reserves, with no reassuring resolution attached.

The Dead End is available now on all major digital platforms. Listen to the EP below and order it here.

items.title: “Shall I Stroke Your Fragile Ego?” — Industrial Darkwave Duo IARA NAGA Take Aim at Scene Power Games in Video for “Big Fish”
items.summary: Shall I stroke your fragile ego? Gotta make myself so small for you A little authority in a small music scene can do remarkable things to a person’s sense of… The post “Shall I Stroke Your Fragile Ego?” — Industrial Darkwave Duo IARA NAGA Take Aim at Scene Pow
items.fullText:
Shall I stroke your fragile ego?
Gotta make myself so small for you 

A little authority in a small music scene can do remarkable things to a person’s sense of proportion. A few contacts become a private kingdom, attention becomes a favour, and everyone else is expected to shrink until the room belongs to one magnificently inflated ego. London/Brighton duo IARA NAGA have apparently run out of patience with this particular species.

Comprising producers Shonalika and Danny Sanchez, the pair unveil the video for their debut single Big Fish. Released on October 22, 2026, through Gasolina Recordings, the track takes aim at the abuse of power within niche communities, where supposed solidarity can become a convenient cover for somebody’s considerable appetite for control.

A jackhammer drumbeat opens proceedings, accompanied by bass-heavy synth waves that buck and warble around the rhythm. Old-school Ministry and Nine Inch Nails offer useful points of reference, while the production brings that industrial attack into contact with contemporary darkwave. An anxious bounce runs through the percussion and electronics, suggesting a stray mid-1990s alternative single passed between an industrial club and an adventurous radio programmer. Everything stays lean enough for each accusation to land.

The vocal sits somewhere between Shirley Manson’s caustic poise and Justine Frischmann’s conversational bite, delivered with a sneer so dry it could strip the paint from a dressing-room door. Distortion roughens the refrain, giving its wounded accusation an agitated edge as the beat keeps pressing forward. The words fit tightly against that rhythm, turning resentment into something sharply articulated and perversely catchy.

The lyrics pick apart the small humiliations that keep a scene hierarchy intact: flattering a fragile ego, shrinking yourself to preserve somebody else’s importance, and being expected to feel grateful for scraps of attention. The person causing the hurt claims the injured party’s role, shifting blame onto whoever has absorbed their behaviour. Painful truths are buried to preserve the group’s good time, while walking away becomes the clearest escape from an arrangement designed to make one person lose.

The video gives that inflated ego suitably extravagant accommodation. Red walls, heavy curtains, an ornate gold mirror, and a lavish bed surround a heavily made-up figure whose attention moves between their own reflection and a phone screen. Fishnet, leather, elaborate cosmetics, and bedside encounters turn the room into a little court of appearances, with social-media posts intruding on the action. Elsewhere, two elaborately dressed characters compare messages and comfort one another.

A public apology delivers the ugliest punchline: an announcement of accountability swiftly turns into an account of the writer’s own suffering and personal growth. The person supposedly accepting responsibility remains, unmistakably, at the centre of the frame. Against this bedroom drama, IARA NAGA performs before a bare white-brick wall, their movements casting vast silhouettes across it. When the figure from the red room finally curls onto the floor, the song’s portrait of fragile authority finds its starkly literal form.

Watch the video for Big Fish below:

Formed in the summer of 2026 following the end of Death Drive, IARA NAGA takes its name from shape-shifting figures in Indian and Brazilian folklore, reflecting the producers’ respective heritages. Moving through synthpop, punk, darkwave, percussive industrial, and EBM, the project probes identity, marginalisation, and corruption. Urban decay, neo-noir, magical realism, and survival shape its world.

Big Fish was produced by IARA NAGA and mixed by Jack Milwaukee (M!R!M).

items.title: Irîs signs to Ethereal Projector for ‘Dystopian Ambient Soundscapes’
items.summary: Luxembourg dark ambient project Irîs has signed to US label Ethereal Projector, with debut release "The Earth Looked Up And Cried" due December 4, 2026.
items.fullText:
Luxembourg-based dark ambient project Irîs has signed to US label Ethereal Projector for a series of releases billed as “Dystopian Ambient Soundscapes.” The first release under the deal, “The Earth Looked Up And Cried,” a title referencing Virgin Prunes, is scheduled for December 4, 2026.

Ethereal Projector’s Bandcamp roster includes Portal of Reflections, Lastboss, la05un, Hyenas for Sale, Fonolabe and Akira Film Script. The label had not yet listed “The Earth Looked Up And Cried” as of the announcement.

Irîs describes its music as blending ambient and experimental electronic elements with neoclassical, drone, minimalism, noise, industrial and electroacoustic components, filed under the project’s own “Dystopian Ambient Soundscapes” banner. Many of Irîs’s compositions, recorded since February 2023, are done in one take, without multitracking or overdubs.

Irîs’s back catalogue on Bandcamp

Irîs’s debut album, “First Journey,” was released on vinyl in April 2025 as a hand-numbered edition of 325 copies pressed via Objects Manufacturing in Berlin, distributed across Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, France and Portugal, alongside a digital edition on Bandcamp. Two further digital-only releases followed on the same page: “The Robot Wars (Variations In C2),” described as the soundtrack to a virtual film or video game, and “Land Of The Rising Sun,” released in February 2026.

In July 2026, Irîs released a collaborative album with Chilean electronic artist Marcelo Diaz Soto (Madsrecords) under the name mirîad. “Amber Starforest (A Viridian Suite in 5 Movements)” comprises five tracks: “The Great Space Migration,” “Nested Dreams During Cryostasis,” “Echoes Of Tycho’s Supernova,” “Amber Starforest” and “The Pillars Of Creation,” running between roughly 18 and 37 minutes each.

Irîs has also released tracks via Dodendans, a Rotterdam-based label that issues regular horror- and urban-legend-themed compilations, and via the Institute For Alien Research (IFAR) label in Bath, UK, where Irîs’s contributions run a symbolic 4 minutes 33 seconds each, a reference to John Cage’s 1952 composition “4’33”.”

About Irîs

Irîs is a dark ambient and experimental electronic project based in Luxembourg, active since February 2023. Its music combines ambient and electronic production with neoclassical, drone, minimalist, noise, industrial and electroacoustic elements, filed by the project under the banner “Dystopian Ambient Soundscapes.”

Irîs released its debut album, “First Journey,” on vinyl in April 2025, followed by the digital-only “The Robot Wars (Variations In C2)” and, in February 2026, “Land Of The Rising Sun.” Irîs has also contributed tracks to Dodendans, a Rotterdam-based compilation label, and to the Institute For Alien Research in Bath, UK. In July 2026, Irîs released the collaborative album “Amber Starforest (A Viridian Suite in 5 Movements)” with Chilean artist Marcelo Diaz Soto under the project name mirîad, and later that month released an accompanying comic magazine made with artist Marc Jost. Since the summer of 2024, Irîs has also shown abstract visual works, based on photography, in individual and group exhibitions in Belgium and Luxembourg.

Irîs’s first release for Ethereal Projector, “The Earth Looked Up And Cried,” is scheduled for December 4, 2026, opening a new “Dystopian Ambient Soundscapes” chapter for the project.

items.title: Angermund sets ‘Fractions’ album for Tellé Records
items.summary: Norwegian electronic artist Angermund releases the album "Fractions" via Tellé Records on November 27, 2026, led by the single "Hitting The Surface."
items.fullText:
Bergen, Norway-based electronic artist Angermund will release the album ‘Fractions’ via Tellé Records on November 27, 2026. The lead single, “Hitting The Surface,” was released October 16, 2026, and a second single, “Surrender,” is set for November 6.

“Fractions” runs seven tracks: “Defracted,” “Hitting The Surface,” “Collapsing Breath,” “Surrender,” “The More We Want,” “Never Have I” and “While Waiting For Vetle.” “Hitting The Surface” is credited to composer Henrik Angermund.

Angermund’s sound moves between dub, deep techno, melodic trance and indie electronics, with stated influences including Beck, Röyksopp, Bjørn Torske, Four Tet, The Cure and Joy Division. Press materials for “Fractions” describe it as unfolding “like a journey through shifting landscapes, both physical and emotional,” and credit the weather, landscapes and atmosphere of Bergen, along with the artist’s trail running in the surrounding mountains, as part of the creative process.

“Hitting The Surface” is available as a digital track on Spotify.

About Angermund

Angermund is an electronic music project based in Bergen, Norway. The project’s sound draws on dub, deep techno, melodic trance and indie electronics, with stated reference points including Beck, Röyksopp, Bjørn Torske, Four Tet, The Cure and Joy Division.

Angermund’s debut album for Tellé Records, “Fractions,” is set for release on November 27, 2026. Its lead single, “Hitting The Surface,” composed by Henrik Angermund, arrived October 16, 2026, ahead of the album’s second single, “Surrender,” due November 6. Angermund credits Bergen’s changing weather, landscapes and atmosphere, along with his own trail running in the mountains around the city, as part of the album’s creative process.

items.title: T.A.N.K. releases video for ‘Bloodsucker (R010R Cover)’
items.summary: T.A.N.K. has released an official video for "Bloodsucker (R010R Cover)," an exclusive bonus track from the Bandcamp edition of "Broken Mirror."
items.fullText:
German EBM project T.A.N.K. released an official video for ‘Bloodsucker (R010R Cover)’ on October 21, 2026, via Electro Aggression Records. The track is described as an exclusive bonus Bandcamp track, added to the digital edition of T.A.N.K.’s third album, “Broken Mirror” (EAR 019), released May 30, 2026.

“Bloodsucker (R010R Cover)” is a cover of a song by Electro Aggression Records labelmate R010R. It is the 18th and final track on the Bandcamp listing for “Broken Mirror,” distinct from T.A.N.K.’s own original song “Bloodsucker,” which appears earlier in the tracklist. “Broken Mirror” otherwise runs 18 tracks across the core album and a set of remixes, including versions by Pyrroline, Sleepwalk, Serpents, Synaptic Defect and Trilogy.

T.A.N.K. is the solo EBM project of Reinhard Hüber, who previously played in the early-1990s East German post-punk band Faust before launching T.A.N.K. in 2001. “Broken Mirror” is his third album as T.A.N.K., following T.A.N.K.’s 2003 debut “Musica Naturale” and 2017’s “Return.”

“Broken Mirror” is available as a digital album and CD via Electro Aggression Records.

About T.A.N.K.

T.A.N.K. is the solo EBM project of Reinhard Hüber, who played in the early-1990s East German post-punk band Faust before launching T.A.N.K. in 2001. The project’s name is an acronym for “Taktischer Angriff (auf’s) Nervenkostüm” (tactical assault on the nervous system). Hüber played his first show as T.A.N.K. at the inaugural Electric Tremor Festival in Dessau, Germany, on March 22, 2002.

T.A.N.K.’s debut album, “Musica Naturale,” followed in 2003 on Ars Electrique, featuring the songs “Freakshow” and “Electroheart.” The album drew the attention of Nader Moumneh, head of Electro Aggression Records, who invited Hüber to contribute the song “Game of Men” to the label’s “Old School Electrology (OSE) Vol. I” compilation (EAR 001). A second T.A.N.K. album, “Return,” followed in 2017.

Hüber later rejoined the Electro Aggression Records roster, contributing remixes to R010R’s “Total Disinformation Awareness” (EAR 015) and Synaptic Defect’s “Initializing Insanity” (EAR 017), both 2CD releases on the label. T.A.N.K.’s third album, “Broken Mirror” (EAR 019), followed on May 30, 2026, with the “Bloodsucker (R010R Cover)” bonus track added to its Bandcamp edition in October 2026. R010R previously spoke to Side-Line in a Click Interview.

items.title: Sky Problem signs to Géographie, releases self-titled single
items.summary: Paris trio Sky Problem has signed to Géographie and released the single "Sky Problem," the first taste of a debut EP due in early 2027.
items.fullText:
The Paris-based electronic/trip-hop trio Sky Problem has signed to Géographie and released its self-titled debut single, ‘Sky Problem’, on October 22, 2026. The track is the first preview of the band’s debut EP, due in early 2027.

The group comprises Gaëlle Croguennec, Kevin Coeur-Joly, and Ricardo Lepoutre and formed in Paris in 2025. Géographie’s roster also includes Marble Arch, The Bernadette Maries, Dog Park, Good Morning TV, and Bad Pelicans. Side-Line previously covered label act SCHØØL’s ‘Gardener’ in 2025.

Sky Problem wrote, composed, recorded and mixed the track themselves, with additional guitars from Gaultier and beats from Clement Hateau. Phoebe Bentham handled assistant recording at Brighton Electric Studios, and Marco Pellegrino mastered the track at Analog Cut. The single, which runs five minutes and 34 seconds, combines trip-hop rhythm with downtempo electronic production.

“Sky Problem” is available as a digital track on Bandcamp.

About Sky Problem

Sky Problem formed in Paris in 2025 as a trio of Gaëlle Croguennec, Kevin Coeur-Joly, and Ricardo Lepoutre. The project’s self-titled single, released October 22, 2026, is its first release since signing to the Paris label Géographie, also home to Marble Arch, The Bernadette Maries, SCHØØL, Dog Park, Good Morning TV, and Bad Pelicans. The single was written, composed, recorded and mixed by the band, with guitars from Gaultier and beats from Clement Hateau, assistant-recorded by Phoebe Bentham at Brighton Electric Studios and mastered by Marco Pellegrino at Analog Cut. A six-track debut EP is due via Géographie in early 2027.

items.title: Ana Palindrome signs to World of Echo, shares ‘A Man A Cure’
items.summary: Irish art-pop trio Ana Palindrome has signed to World of Echo and released the single "A Man A Cure," with a debut album expected in early 2027.
items.fullText:
Irish experimental art-pop trio Ana Palindrome has signed to World of Echo and released the single ‘A Man A Cure’. The signing was announced alongside the single and an accompanying video, timed to two UK support dates with labelmates Tara Clerkin Trio.

“A Man A Cure” was recorded across bedrooms, wardrobes and homemade vocal booths. The lyrics question the idea that anyone can be entirely “self-made” or independent, a theme the group connects to the character of “Ana Palindrome” that it has built around the project. The video, a visualiser, offers a first look at that character. Ana Palindrome joined Tara Clerkin Trio for two sold-out UK dates, at London’s ICA on October 21 and at Halle St Peters in Manchester on October 22. A debut album is expected in early 2027.

About Ana Palindrome

Ana Palindrome is an Irish experimental art-pop trio and the newest signing to the UK label World of Echo. “A Man A Cure” is the group’s first release since signing to the label, recorded with a do-it-yourself approach and centred on a fictional lead character the band has created under the same name. World of Echo also represents Tara Clerkin Trio, whose UK tour dates Ana Palindrome joined this week in London and Manchester. The label has announced a debut Ana Palindrome album for early 2027, with further details expected to follow.

items.title: Purwien & Kowa release sixth album ‘Sechs’ on October 23
items.summary: Purwien & Kowa release their sixth album "Sechs" on October 23 via Town and Towers, produced by Olaf Wollschläger, on Bandcamp, digital and CD.
items.fullText:
German-Swiss synthpop duo Purwien & Kowa releases their sixth studio album, ‘Sechs’, on October 23, 2026, via Town and Towers. The eleven-track album was produced by Olaf Wollschläger and is available on Bandcamp, digitally and on CD.

The tracklist comprises “Italo-disco in San Francisco” in both German and English versions, “Concorde (12″ Mix),” “Hinter Glas,” “Bandit 2000,” “Gravity,” “System,” “We’re Wrong,” “Eyes of Aragon,” “Irgendwas ist immer” and “Me and My Synthex.” “Hinter Glas” was written by Andreas Sippel and Christian Purwien for Second Decay, Purwien’s former band, while “Eyes of Aragon” was written by Thomas Kowa for his former band No Comment. Christian Purwien sings lead vocals throughout, with Kowa joining him on “Me and My Synthex.”

Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa are also the duo behind Heldautomat, whose own album “Zwischen den Lichtern” is released the same week. Side-Line previously covered two advance singles from “Sechs”: “Hinter Glas”, released ahead of the album, and “Italo-disco in San Francisco”.

About Purwien & Kowa

Purwien & Kowa is a German-Swiss electronic duo based in Dortmund, formed by Christian Purwien and Thomas Kowa. Purwien previously fronted Second Decay, and “Hinter Glas” on “Sechs” revisits a song he co-wrote for that band with Andreas Sippel. Kowa’s former band No Comment is similarly represented on the album through “Eyes of Aragon.” Purwien and Kowa also record together as Heldautomat, a parallel project whose album “Zwischen den Lichtern” arrives the same week as “Sechs.” The duo alternates between the two projects while also running the Disko80 podcast. “Sechs” is Purwien & Kowa’s sixth studio album, produced by Olaf Wollschläger and released through Town and Towers, following the advance singles “Hinter Glas” and “Italo-disco in San Francisco.”

items.title: Heldautomat sets ‘Zwischen den Lichtern’ album for October 23
items.summary: Heldautomat releases the album "Zwischen den Lichtern" on October 23 via Town & Towers Records, produced by Olaf Wollschläger, on Bandcamp and streaming.
items.fullText:
German synthpop duo Heldautomat releases the album ‘Zwischen den Lichtern’ on October 23, 2026, via Town & Towers Records. The ten-track album was produced by Olaf Wollschläger and is available on Bandcamp and major streaming platforms.

The tracklist comprises “Liebe ist endlich,” “Am ersten Tag,” “Anders sein,” “Page of my diary,” “Und jetzt,” “It always rains in Berlin,” “Ungesagt,” “The grass is greener,” “Hurt” and “Manchmal.” “Hurt” is a cover of the Nine Inch Nails song written by Trent Reznor, with piano by Eugene Kazantsev. “Anders sein” was written by Andreas Sippel and Christian Purwien for Second Decay, Purwien’s former band, and is reinterpreted here in Heldautomat’s own electronic arrangement. “Page of my diary” features additional vocals by Molly Gavin, and “The grass is greener” includes a child choir performance by the Ray M. School Choir from Sydney, Australia, and Sophia Chiandusso.

Heldautomat is the duo of Christian Purwien on vocals and lyrics and Thomas Kowa on synthesizers and songwriting. Side-Line has tracked the album’s lead-up through three advance singles: “Am ersten Tag”, the project’s debut single; “Anders Sein”; and “Liebe ist endlich”, all now folded into “Zwischen den Lichtern.”

About Heldautomat

Heldautomat is a German electronic duo based in Dortmund, built around analogue synthesizers, piano, a drum machine and the vocals of Christian Purwien. Purwien previously fronted Second Decay, and “Anders sein” on the new album revisits a song he co-wrote for that band with Andreas Sippel. Purwien and Kowa also record together as Purwien & Kowa, a separate synthpop project that released the single “Hinter Glas” ahead of their own album “Sechs,” and the single “Italo-disco in San Francisco”. Heldautomat’s “Zwischen den Lichtern” was released through Town & Towers Records following the advance singles “Am ersten Tag,” “Anders Sein” and “Liebe ist endlich,” and was produced by Olaf Wollschläger.

items.title: TOXIK Dementia releases ‘Queen of Darkness’ single

Buenos Aires aggrotech and dark electro project TOXIK Dementia has released the single ‘Queen of Darkness’, featuring Ruchia. The track is out now on Bandcamp and is set to reach other platforms on October 31.

TOXIK Dementia is a solo electronic music project led by Abril Rainbow, based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. items.title: Zeromancer confirmed for M’era Luna 2027
items.summary: Zeromancer have been confirmed for M'era Luna 2027 in Hildesheim, ahead of their Testimonial Tour 2027, six German club shows running February 26 to March 13.
items.fullText:
Norwegian industrial rock band Zeromancer have been confirmed for M’era Luna 2027. The festival announced the band as part of its second wave of artists on October 20, with Zeromancer set to perform in Hildesheim, Germany, on either August 7 or 8, 2027. Their exact performance day has not yet been announced.

The M’era Luna booking comes ahead of a run of German club dates. Zeromancer will return to German stages for the first time in eight years with their Testimonial Tour 2027, six shows between February 26 and March 13, with Czech electro-rock band Lakeside X joining as support.

Formed in 1999, Zeromancer have built a catalogue of industrial rock built on heavy guitars, electronics and melodic songwriting, with tracks including “Clone Your Lover”, “Doctor Online” and “Need You Like a Drug” among the band’s best-known. Tour dates and tickets for the Testimonial Tour 2027 are available via Eventim.

Zeromancer’s 2027 touring plans

The M’era Luna booking adds to a run of live activity Side-Line has tracked for Zeromancer this year, including the announcement of the Testimonial Tour 2027 club dates. The festival slot gives the band a second major German appearance in the same year, alongside the six-date club run.

About Zeromancer

Zeromancer is a Norwegian industrial rock band formed in 1999, taking shape in Los Angeles after the Norwegian rock band Seigmen split in January 2000. Several of Zeromancer’s core members, including bassist Kim Ljung, came from Seigmen. The band’s current lineup comprises Alex Moklebust on vocals, Kim Ljung on bass and backing vocals, Noralf Ronthi on drums, Lorry Kristiansen on keyboards and programming since 2003, and Per-Olav Wiik on guitar since 2018.

Zeromancer released its debut album “Clone Your Lover” on March 13, 2000, followed by “Eurotrash” (2001) and “Zzyzx” (2003), largely through Cleopatra Records. Later albums, including “Sinners International” (2009), “The Death of Romance” (2010), “Bye-Bye Borderline” (2013) and “Orchestra of Knives” (2021), were released through Trisol Music Group. Tracks including “Clone Your Lover”, “Doctor Online” and “Need You Like a Drug” remain staples of the band’s live sets. The M’era Luna booking for 2027, alongside the band’s Testimonial Tour 2027 club dates with Lakeside X, marks the band’s first full return to German stages in eight years.

items.title: Metropolis Records reissues VNV Nation’s ‘Noire’ and ‘Electric Sun’ on vinyl
items.summary: Metropolis Records has reissued VNV Nation's "Noire" and "Electric Sun" on vinyl, alongside new pressings for The Tear Garden and 16Volt.
items.fullText:
Metropolis Records has reissued five titles from its catalogue on limited edition coloured vinyl, among them two VNV Nation albums, The Tear Garden‘s “The Brown Acid Caveat” and two 16Volt records.

The VNV Nation pressings cover two different periods of the Irish-German electronic group’s catalogue. “Noire”, originally released in 2018, is the band’s 10th album, a release built around dark-and-light contrasts, melodic dance beats and post-classical soundtrack pieces. Its 2023 follow-up, “Electric Sun”, arrives in the same reissue wave. Both are pressed on clear 2xLP vinyl. Metropolis Records holds North American rights to VNV Nation’s catalogue, and the reissues are being sold through the label for that territory.

“The Brown Acid Caveat” gets a tangerine vinyl pressing timed to the first North American tour by The Tear Garden, the occasional side project of cEvin Key (Skinny Puppy) and Edward Ka-Spel (The Legendary Pink Dots). The album was originally released in 2017 as the duo’s eighth full-length under that name and marked 30 years of the pair’s collaboration.

The two 16Volt reissues, “Skin” (1994) and “LetDownCrush” (1996), were both produced by band founder Eric Powell alongside Keith Auerbach and Jeff Newell, who have also worked with Ministry and Angels & Airwaves. “Skin” was the band’s sophomore album; “LetDownCrush” followed two years later. The new pressings are on red and yellow vinyl respectively.

All five titles are available now through Metropolis Records and its retail partners.

VNV Nation’s reissue history with Metropolis

VNV Nation has been on Side-Line’s radar for years, most recently with a look back at their album “Automatic” on its anniversary. The band, led by Ronan Harris, has built its catalogue steadily since the 1990s, and Metropolis Records has periodically returned to that catalogue for vinyl reissues as demand for physical formats has grown.

16Volt has had a similarly active relationship with the label in 2026: Metropolis released a remastered edition of the band’s debut album, “Wisdom”, and issued the “NegativeOnArrivals” album on vinyl, following an earlier CD-only release. The “Skin” and “LetDownCrush” vinyl pressings extend that reissue campaign further back into Eric Powell’s catalogue.

About VNV Nation

VNV Nation was founded by Ronan Harris in Leeds, England, in 1990, initially as a solo electronic project before relocating to Ireland. Mark Jackson joined as live drummer, and the band went on to release a long run of albums on Metropolis Records and Anachron Sound, including “Empires” (1999), “Futureperfect” (2006) and “Automatic” (2011), building a following across the electronic, EBM and futurepop scenes. “Noire”, released in 2018 as the band’s 10th studio album, combined the group’s melodic dance material with more cinematic, orchestral passages. “Electric Sun” followed in 2023, drawing on both vintage and modern analog synthesizers. The Metropolis vinyl reissues of both albums bring that catalogue back into physical circulation alongside new pressings for labelmates The Tear Garden and 16Volt.

Dark Force Fest 2027 full lineup

The pre-party on Thursday, April 29 takes place with Lost Signal.

Where to attend Dark Force Fest 2027 and buy tickets

About Dark Force Fest

Dark Force Fest is a three-day goth-industrial and dark-alternative festival and convention created by VampireFreaks and held at the Sheraton Parsippany Hotel. The festival grew out of earlier VampireFreaks events such as Dark Side of the Con and Triton Festival and is promoted as one of North America’s largest gatherings dedicated to industrial, goth, post-punk, darkwave and related genres.

VampireFreaks announced the first Dark Force Fest in 2022 for its 2023 debut, then unveiled the 2024 edition with an expanded format. The 2026 lineup was confirmed in September 2025, and daily headliners Combichrist, Front Line Assembly and London After Midnight were announced in January 2026 for that May edition. The 2027 edition follows the same three-night, multi-headliner format that has defined the festival since its 2023 debut.

items.title: The Sisters of Mercy’s ‘Vision Thing’ turns 36 on 22 October
items.summary: The Sisters of Mercy's third album "Vision Thing" turns 36 on 22 October. The gothic rock record was produced by Andrew Eldritch and Jim Steinman.
items.fullText:
The Sisters of Mercy’s third studio album, “Vision Thing,” turns 36 on 22 October. Merciful Release and East West Records released the gothic rock record in the UK on 22 October 1990, with Elektra Records handling distribution in the US.

Andrew Eldritch produced the album, sharing the credit with Jim Steinman on the track “More” and with Chris Tsangarides on “When You Don’t See Me.” The band recorded “Vision Thing” over nine months at Puk Recording Studios in Gjerlev, Denmark. Eldritch wrote or co-wrote all eight tracks, which run: “Vision Thing,” “Ribbons,” “Detonation Boulevard,” “Something Fast,” “When You Don’t See Me,” “Doctor Jeep,” “More” and “I Was Wrong,” totaling 42 minutes and 35 seconds.

The lineup on the record featured Eldritch on vocals, guitars and keyboards, alongside guitarists Tim Bricheno and Andreas Bruhn, bassist Tony James and the band’s drum machine, Doktor Avalanche. Guitarist John Perry, who had turned down a full-time role in the band, contributed guitar and slide guitar on “Detonation Boulevard” as a guest, and Maggie Reilly sang backing vocals on five of the eight tracks. “Vision Thing” reached number 11 on the UK Albums Chart and was certified Silver by the BPI, and it later went Gold in Germany. Merciful Release reissued the album in November 2006 with five bonus tracks, including the non-album single “You Could Be the One.”

About The Sisters of Mercy

The Sisters of Mercy formed in Leeds, England, in 1980 around Andrew Eldritch and guitarist Gary Marx, later joined by guitarist Ben Gunn and bassist Craig Adams, with a drum machine the band named Doktor Avalanche standing in for a live drummer from the start. The band built its following through a run of independent singles on its own Merciful Release label before signing to WEA/East West for wider distribution. Its 1985 debut album, “First and Last and Always,” established the band within the emerging gothic rock scene, followed by 1987’s “Floodland,” which included the singles “This Corrosion” and “Dominion/Mother Russia” and featured bassist Patricia Morrison. Morrison left the band by the end of 1989, and former Sigue Sigue Sputnik member Tony James joined on bass as the band, now also featuring new guitarist Andreas Bruhn and later Tim Bricheno, prepared its third album. “Vision Thing,” released on 22 October 1990, closed out the band’s studio album releases to date; The Sisters of Mercy have continued to tour and perform new unreleased material live in the years since without issuing another studio record.

items.title: Aetherium Nebula releases second album ‘Ephemeral Port’ via Cryo Chamber
items.summary: Aetherium Nebula releases its second album, "Ephemeral Port," on Cryo Chamber, a nine-track cyberpunk dark ambient record featuring Maris Anguis.
items.fullText:
Aetherium Nebula, the cyberpunk-themed dark ambient project of Baltimore, Maryland musician Dan Barrett, has released its second full-length album, “Ephemeral Port”, on 20 October through Cryo Chamber. The nine-track record places the listener as a cybernetically enhanced resident of a dystopian city receiving a cyberware update through a maintenance terminal.

Barrett wrote all nine tracks, co-writing “Dismantling The Outer Shell” with Henrik Karlsson of Subverge. Vocals on the opening two tracks come from Ryo Utasato, the Japanese-born, Chicago-based artist who records as Maris Anguis.

  2. Source Code Unfurling As Myriad Spiraling Arms (feat. Maris Anguis)
  3. Sunken Below The Physical Layer
  4. Wreckage Upon The Datastream
  5. Nanoscaffolding
  6. Dismantling The Outer Shell (feat. Subverge)
  7. A Thousand Artificial Wounds To Mend
  8. Disposal – Initiate System Regen
  9. Upgrade Complete

“Ephemeral Port” is available as a digital album and as a CD limited to 200 copies in a six-panel digipak designed by Simon Heath, the Cryo Chamber founder also known for Atrium Carceri. The CD edition ships to the US and EU.

“Ephemeral Port” follows two story cycles Aetherium Nebula built through 2026: the Dhuna-Rhim series, which began with the single “Erased” in July and continued with “Personality Disorder” in August, and the ArcSec City cycle, spanning “ArcSec City I,” “Six Sorrows: ArcSec City II,” the “Separation” EP, the single “Sewage” and the “Memorywipe” EP. The standalone single “Pale Sunlight,” released in June, bridged the two cycles. Barrett and Karlsson also co-founded the Arcane Dirge imprint, which released Maris Anguis’s album “Pilgrimage of Fire” in October 2025.

About Aetherium Nebula

Dan Barrett, also known for the dark ambient project Worms of the Earth, runs Aetherium Nebula out of Baltimore, Maryland. The project describes itself as a “dark and emotive cyberpunk-themed multimedia project”, built around interconnected literary works and their soundtracks that explore isolation and the search for purpose in a hostile, mechanized future. The project released its debut album, “Glacialis Mundi”, through Winter-Light in August 2023.

Barrett spent 2026 extending the project’s fiction across two parallel story cycles, the Dhuna-Rhim series and the ArcSec City cycle, released as a run of singles and EPs, before returning to a full-length with “Ephemeral Port” on Cryo Chamber on 20 October. The new album carries Aetherium Nebula’s cybernetic dystopia into its most extensive single release to date, with vocal and writing contributions from Maris Anguis and Subverge’s Henrik Karlsson.

items.summary: Slovak cybermetal band Khadaver will release its third album, "Xaosblack," on 13 November on its own Khadaver Industries imprint, with a Gloom feature.
items.fullText:
Khadaver, the Slovak cybermetal project led by guitarist, composer and programmer Nihil Nix, will release its third full-length album, “Xaosblack,” on 13 November through the band’s own Khadaver Industries imprint. The record addresses modern dystopia, surveillance, disinformation and corporate power eroding trust in the systems meant to counter them.

Nihil Nix produced, recorded and mixed “Xaosblack” at Xi Studio, with mastering by Marek Kula. The eleven-track album is available for pre-order in digital and CD formats on Bandcamp. The title track carries a guest vocal performance from Martin Pazdera of the Slovak gothic metal band Gloom.

The CD edition adds three bonus tracks: a re-recorded version of “Re:Animate” (2021), the S/M Infusion remix of “High-Tech Genocide,” and a cover of Fear Factory‘s “New Breed,” originally from “Demanufacture” (1995).

“Xaosblack” is the first Khadaver album with the lineup of vocalist Arion Mars and drummer Sineon Nighthorn, who joined in 2024, and bassist Madness, who joined in June 2026 after founding-era bassist Attar IX departed. The single “Human Disposal Limited,” released 4 October with a video directed by Nihil Nix, preceded the album announcement.

About Khadaver

Nihil Nix formed Khadaver in Slovakia in 2006. The project’s first demo, “Beta Version,” appeared in 2008 and won the Top Demo award from the Dutch webzine Alternate Zone. A second demo, “GOD-RW,” followed in 2010. Khadaver released its debut album, “New World Disorder,” in August 2012, and a second album, “Exstinctio Mundi,” in November 2015, before lineup difficulties and a shortage of live shows pushed the band into inactivity in 2016.

Nihil Nix revived Khadaver as a solo project in 2021, marking the band’s 15th anniversary with the rarities collection “DMZ: Demos & Rarities” and the single “Re:Animate.” A full band returned in 2024 with vocalist Arion Mars, bassist Attar IX and drummer Sineon Nighthorn, releasing the singles “Cypherfiend” and “High-Tech Genocide,” the latter with a music video. Attar IX left in June 2026 and was replaced by bassist Madness, who appears alongside Nihil Nix in the video for “Human Disposal Limited.” That single, released 4 October 2026, set up “Xaosblack,” the first full-length to carry the current lineup and Khadaver’s third album overall, due 13 November on the band’s own Khadaver Industries imprint.

When silence is frightening: Korfian and the art of electronic catharsis

The sound of Korfian’s new single ‘Melodramatic’ is fant­ast­ic­ally elec­tron­ic, as if Björk’s Greek cous­in were at the con­trols, so to speak. Musically, the track oper­ates in the realm of elec­tro (with a touch of synth pop?) and comes across as pleas­antly exper­i­ment­al, but to my taste it stays firmly on track son­ic­ally, without drift­ing into any­thing too com­plex or wild. It’s a very dis­tinct­ive elec­tro sound that doesn’t quite fit into the clas­sic synth-pop mould styl­ist­ic­ally. Whether you find the whole thing unwieldy or catchy prob­ably depends on your own listen­ing habits.

In any case, the song com­pletely won me over from the very first listen. Lyrically, Korfian takes aim at staged suf­fer­ing and tox­ic dynam­ics with his usu­al pre­ci­sion. A cath­artic act of lib­er­a­tion, wrapped in an express­ive elec­tron­ic guise.

items.title: Combichrist – The Venom In The Mouth Of God (Digital/CD/Vinyl Album – Out Of Line)
items.summary: Andy LaPlegua released a new Combichrist album this summer, an event many fans always look...
items.fullText:
Andy LaPlegua released a new Combichrist album this summer, an event many fans always look forward to. I might be making a somewhat unusual comparison here, but the evolution of Combichrist strongly reminds me of the path taken by Dawn Of Ashes. I’m not necessarily comparing the two in terms of genre—although perhaps I am—but both started out with an Electro-inspired sound, gradually moved towards a more pronounced Metal production, and eventually arrived at a synthesis of both influences.

Combichrist already made this clear on their previous album, “CMBCRST”, which was a masterpiece, but on this new record, the fusion is even more explicit. It’s a perfect blend of EBM, Dark-Electro with an Industrial edge, and Metal. Some tracks lean more towards the Electronic side, while others are dominated by guitars. Throughout its 13 tracks, the album delivers top-tier production. The Electronic elements are built around icy, abrasive textures and leads, while the Metal components add an extra punch. And then, of course, there’s Andy’s voice, which once again sounds powerful and possessed. Amid all this intensity, softer passages occasionally emerge, evoking something akin to Industrial-Pop. The album exudes a sense of complete creative freedom, as if nothing is forced and anything is possible. This gives the record a distinctly personal and inventive character.

The album contains several gems and certainly won’t disappoint Combichrist fans. Once again, a brilliant record—made in Norway. (Rating:9).

Listen to “Born Destroyer”:

About Combichrist

Combichrist is an aggrotech and industrial metal project formed in Atlanta, Georgia in 2003 by Norwegian vocalist Andy LaPlegua. LaPlegua had already worked with Icon of Coil, Panzer AG, Scandy and Scandinavian Cock. The studio project is centered on LaPlegua, with a changing live lineup. Current listed members are Andy LaPlegua, Eric13, Elliott Berlin and Jamie Cronander.

The project’s first material developed from the track “Thanx to my Buddies”, originally written under the name D.r.i.v.E. The name later changed to Hudlager and then Combichrist before the debut album “The Joy of Gunz” appeared on Out Of Line in 2003. It was followed by “Kiss The Blade”, also in 2003, “Blut Royale” and “Sex, Drogen Und Industrial” in 2004, and “Get Your Body Beat” in 2006.

The next studio albums included “Everybody Hates You” in 2005, “What the Fuck Is Wrong with You People?” in 2007, “Today We Are All Demons” in 2009, “Making Monsters” in 2010, “No Redemption” in 2013, “We Love You” in 2014, “This Is Where Death Begins” in 2016, “One Fire” in 2019 and “Cmbcrst” in 2024. Note that “No Redemption” was released as the official “DmC: Devil May Cry” soundtrack.

Combichrist’s follow-up to “Cmbcrst”, “The Venom In The Mouth Of God,” was released on July 24, 2026 via Out Of Line Music as digipak CD, Yolk Splatter Vinyl 2LP and Picture Vinyl 2LP, and is reviewed here.

Beyond the performances, the organizers advertise more than 100 vendors, club events, a costume contest, cosplay guests, sideshow performers, activities, and panels. Reminiscing of your kiss
Can I taste your lips so sweet and
Candy Rocks, red and green
When cupid shot another arrow

The American candy shop has always been a magnificent fraud: a place where children are coaxed into lifelong chemical dependencies beneath the reassuring gaze of adults who see nothing strange in selling artificially colored sugar to anyone with a dollar. Somewhere between the taffy machine and the insulin prescription comes the latest confection from Virginia Beach art-rock eccentrics Reptile Tile, who join forces with Los Angeles synth-pop provocateur Geneva Jacuzzi on Candy Boy, a three-song EP concerned with romantic dysfunction, consumer addiction, and the magnificent foolishness of human desire.

Founded in 2015 by Roderick Edens, alias Terry Cloth, Reptile Tile belongs to that wonderfully diseased branch of American musical experimentation populated by Devo, Ween, The Residents, and assorted basement-dwelling lunatics who regard conventional song structures as invitations to commit minor acts of cultural vandalism.

The title track was originally written during the sessions for Jacuzzi’s Triple Fire, released by Dais Records in 2024, and is also slated to appear on Reptile Tile’s forthcoming full-length LP. For now, it heads a compact collaboration whose other two songs, Accessory and Cliche, explore more upbeat synth-pop territory while examining further complications of wanting things that might be bad for you.

A warm, rounded bassline gives Candy Boy its easy sway, while synths chime like softly struck bells through a light haze of electronics. Geneva Jacuzzi sings as though caught halfway between remembering a kiss and imagining the next one, her daydream delivery lending the song a deliciously dazed sweetness. Those airy textures soften the edges of her romantic fixation, making another taste sound like the most reasonable proposition in the world. Cupid, judging by the results, may have started dipping his arrows in something stronger than sugar.

The self-produced video was directed by Reptile Tile’s Andrew Briggs and shot on location in Virginia Beach by Taylor Casey. Its inspirations include neon noir films and the atmosphere of 1990s children’s television shows such as Are You Afraid of the Dark?, an appropriate combination for a story in which a brightly stocked candy shop conceals some highly questionable extracurricular chemistry. The song’s press release offers a useful warning: “Not everything is as it appears in the candy shop…”

Set on the Virginia Beach boardwalk, the video introduces Jacuzzi as an ingénue being tailed by a police officer investigating the rise of illegal “candy” along the strip. Edens plays the mustachioed officer, complete with mirrored sunglasses and a tendency to peer around corners. Jacuzzi, meanwhile, walks past the nighttime storefronts in a black leather jacket worn over her hot-pink strapless gown, an enormous jeweled necklace catching the light beneath her severe black bob. Her attention settles on the officer’s son, played by Lane Wills, a bespectacled candy-store employee whose white shirt and black apron suggest considerably more innocence than his workplace deserves.

Their flirtation develops among shelves of plush animals, oversized sweets, and brightly colored dispensers, with exchanged glances making the merchandise seem increasingly incidental. After their introduction, the Candy Boy leads Jacuzzi behind the counter and through an employees-only door, revealing a secret laboratory run by chemists played by Andrew Briggs and Chris Santiago. Bubbling glassware, clouds of vapor, and bright red, yellow, and blue liquids crowd the workbench as the clerk proudly shows his visitor around. Later close-ups reveal trays of translucent, pistol-shaped sweets, giving the confectionery business a particularly literal criminal accessory.

The laboratory romance alternates with performance scenes in a small room saturated with pink light. Here, Jacuzzi sheds the biker jacket and completes her ensemble with matching opera gloves, jeweled bracelets, and a pink tulle headpiece. The wardrobe pays homage to Madonna’s Material Girl video and, through that reference, Marilyn Monroe’s performance of Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend. Hands planted on her hips, she delivers coy sideways looks and exaggerated gestures at the microphone, bringing Hollywood glamour into considerably stranger company. Behind her, a keyboardist wears a laboratory coat and goggles, while the policeman plays bass, maintaining an admirably flexible interpretation of being on duty.

Back in the laboratory, attraction develops into an embrace before the clerk removes his apron and takes Jacuzzi outside. They emerge hand in hand into a smoke-filled alley, where bright backlighting turns their flirtation into a miniature movie romance. Their encounter against the wall is interrupted when his father appears with a flashlight. Jacuzzi promptly runs toward the camera, leaving the Candy Boy against the building as the pursuit resumes. Whatever the family’s position on illicit confectionery, the young man has chosen a spectacularly inconvenient place for a date.

Soft focus, overlapping images, long dissolves, and prismatic flashes give the action a pleasantly intoxicated appearance. Faces float across storefronts, laboratory colors bleed into romantic close-ups, and the pink performance footage dissolves into the alleyway chase. Glamour, infatuation, and suspicious confectionery all appear to be products of the same highly questionable chemistry experiment.

Reptile Tile and Geneva Jacuzzi give their confectionery caper a conspiratorial twist, posing a few questions best answered before anyone samples another batch:

“The video begs the questions…will the internet pilled generation always do as they’re told by the CIA? Will Geneva and the candy boy fall in love? And lastly, what is the secret ingredient being added to the candy that makes everyone want more?”

Watch the video for Candy Boy below:

Accessory, also co-written and sung by Geneva Jacuzzi, combines 1980s synth-pop with the sentimental architecture of 1950s doo-wop. Bright layers of synthesizer and an insistent beat frame the perspective of a trophy wife who has reached her breaking point, her decorative usefulness having finally exhausted her patience. Its buoyant electronics provide an appropriately ridiculous backdrop for a domestic rebellion, suggesting a suburban house party where somebody has spiked the punch with industrial-strength resentment.

Cliche ventures into heartbreak and self-fulfilling prophecy, its bashful vocal sitting atop a peculiar synth-pop tune surrounded by electronic flourishes and layers of drifting ambience. The band claims every lyric eventually came true, which should concern anybody contemplating writing an entire album about lottery winnings or romantic satisfaction.

The EP was recorded at Reptile Tile’s home studio, RTT Lab, mixed by Stephen Bement at Vox Studios, and mastered by Nick Bolton at Bolton Sounds. Picky Choosy Records is releasing Candy Boy as a digital single across streaming platforms, with a limited-edition magenta 7-inch vinyl release announced as coming soon through Bandcamp and Reptile Tile’s website.

Candy Boy offers three variations on humanity’s curious appetite for things that eventually make us miserable. The candy is suspicious, the relationships are deteriorating, and everybody seems entirely too enthusiastic about returning for another helping. Reptile Tile and Geneva Jacuzzi have concocted an entertaining little racket, exploiting that ancient human weakness for anything attractively packaged and potentially disastrous. The customers are hooked, the cops are closing in, and somewhere in the back room, somebody is already cooking up the next batch.
